punchline: Surgeons wore blood-stiff gowns with pride while Lister cleaned wounds against germs nobody could see.
thirty_sec: In Glasgow in 1865 Joseph Lister had read Pasteur's work on microscopic organisms. When an eleven-year-old boy came in with a compound leg fracture, he dressed it with carbolic acid. The wound did not fester and the leg healed, though many surgeons still resisted for years.
